universe.rule: every part number in bvp_pn_dimension.csv or pms_capture_supplement.csv that carries a pms_category — the whole service-part list, nothing cut off by euro or by batch size

already_carrying_a_family.source: vehicle_family_bands.csv — the cross-reference or the existing decode

still_needing_an_epc_lookup.note: ordered by euro so the highest value is decoded first; nothing is cut off by the batch size, the batch number is a sitting

excluded_placeholder_preamble.note: REBATE, TRANSPORT and similar — not part numbers, the EPC cannot resolve them

defect_this_replaces.effect: cross-reference-known part numbers were dropped from the decode because their family was known, and then dropped from the family view because they were not in the decode
defect_this_replaces.effect_measured: the part numbers the cross-reference names a vehicle for were on neither side; none of them appeared in the decode
defect_this_replaces.earlier_claim_withdrawn: an earlier estimate of 95 heavy-truck-only part numbers at EUR 1,955,749 across eleven service families does not reproduce and is not quoted here; the bare F* substring test behind it read TF*, the D-Max pickup wildcard, as an F-series token, and the euro rested on the blower filters whose model string is TF*,UC* — six part numbers billing EUR 1,347,222.32 on all years, all markets and all billing lines, which vehicle_family_bands.csv places in the Light vehicle family, not heavy truck. Nothing in this worklist computes the corrected size: that measurement belongs to vehicle_family_bands.csv, which carries 164 heavy truck part numbers billing EUR 174,832 in 2025 on a 1,238-vehicle fleet
